content.comment_body: Hello, I'm having significant trouble connecting to [product_name]. I have a [product_name] communication cable, but my laptop doesn't have a COM port. When I try using an ExpressCard-COM adapter or a USB-COM adapter, the software becomes unresponsive or even crashes with a blue screen. Where is the issue and how can I solve it? Please assist me. Apologies for my English. Best regards, [user_name].
Hello, The best option is to use the [product_name] USB programming cable. Many USB-to-RS232 converters tend to cause issues. Hope this helps.

Hi [user_name], Here’s another suggestion: 1) Uninstall the USB-RS232 converter cable and disconnect it; 2) Turn off or disable all Bluetooth adapters or built-in devices that might be using COM ports; 3) Restart your computer; 4) Install the USB-COM converter driver before connecting the cable; 5) Plug in the cable and check in Control Panel, under Device Manager and Ports, that the USB/COM converter is assigned a COM port number 5 or lower; 6) Try communicating with [product_name]; 7) Afterwards, you can reactivate Bluetooth devices, which will use COM ports above the one assigned to the [product_name] cable. This has resolved the issue for some users. Cheers!

analysis.insight_summary: Several users are experiencing challenges connecting their laptops to [product_name] using USB or ExpressCard-to-COM adapters, leading to software failures or system crashes. These issues are mostly related to driver conflicts or incorrect COM port assignments when using hardware converters, which affects reliability and usability.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking for straightforward and stable communication between [product_name] and their laptop via common adapter hardware, without encountering driver or troubleshooting problems.
